answer: The farrier logs every shoe, every hoof and every horse at the forge, and the book is read at the fair. A lagoon shoe nailed by a stranger fails the book: at the mesa of the hoof the nail holes must match the farrier's own pattern, and a strange shoe lames the horse. Faking a shoeing record means bribing a farrier, forging a year of entries and paying 7,700, and the dawn entry in the forge book follows the horse, so a horse whose shoes were never logged is barred from the fair.
